# ORAL MUCOSA OR INFECTED SKIN SURGICAL SITE ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS Antimicrobial prophylaxis is indicated in procedures involving oral mucosa or infected skin when the patient is at high risk of infective endocarditis or hematogenous prosthetic joint infection.

**St. Cloud Guidance (Inpatient):**

RECOMMENDATIONS NOT AVAILABLE
Recommendations for this condition are not available within CDSS. Please refer to facility guidelines or other clinical resources for recommendations.

**Minneapolis Guidance:**

Infective endocarditis high risk conditions:

1. Prosthetic cardiac valve
2. Previous infective endocarditis
3. Congenital heart disease
4. Cardiac transplantation recipients who develop vasculopathy
1. First two years following joint replacement
2. Previous prosthetic joint infection
3. Immunocompromised
4. Insulin dependent diabetes
5. HIV infection
6. Malignancy
7. Malnutrition
8. Hemophilia

Oral mucosa surgical site
Amoxicillin 2 gm PO 60 minutes before incision ($) [R]
Unable to take oral medications
Cefazolin 1 gm IV over 30 minutes beginning 60 minutes before incision ($) [R]
< OR >
Ampicillin 2 gm IV over 30 minutes, beginning 60 minutes before incision ($$) [R]
Infected skin surgical site
Cephalexin 1 gm PO 60 minutes before incision ($) [R]
< OR >
Dicloxacillin 2 gm PO 60 minutes before incision ($) [DI]
Unable to take oral medications
Cefazolin 1 gm IV over 30 minutes beginning 60 minutes before incison ($) [R]
Penicillin allergy
Azithromycin 500 mg PO 60 minutes before incision ($) [M]
Unable to take oral medications
Clindamycin 600 mg IV over 30 minutes, 60 minutes before incision ($$) [H,O]
MRSA risk factors
Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO 60 minutes before incision ($) [R,DI] < AND > Penicillin VK 500 mg PO 60 minutes before incision ($) [R]
Unable to take oral medications
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV 120 minutes before incision ($) [R]
